newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin says Aug exports show improving sign.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin says Aug exports show improving sign.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda said on Wednesday Thai exports performed better in August by posting positive year-on-year growth after they declined in value in the previous two months.
Bodi told reporters the improved August export performance coincided with a satisfactory import slowdown. He did not give export figures for July or August.
"I believe economic figures in the remaining four months of this year will stay on an improving trend especially for exports," the minister said.

Thai exports fell 9.5 percent year-on-year to 109.5 billion baht in June. The Bank of Thailand estimated in late August that July exports grew 5.2 percent year-on-year but it is expected to revise that down on Thursday.
Thai exports in the first seven months grew 3.8 percent year-on-year, against a 26.2 percent rise in the same year-ago period.

Bodi, who expects to be replaced after Thailand's ruling six party coalition chooses a new prime minister to succeed Banharn Silpa-archa, said he is prepared to approve any central bank proposals for curbing inflows of short-term foreign funds.
"I would promptly approve measures to control short-term funds...if they are deemed necessary and beneficial (to the country)," he said.

Moody's Investors Service early this month downgraded Thailand's short-term debt rating to Prime-2 from Prime-1, saying its growing short-term debts this year could expose the country to unexpected shocks in the balance of payments.
